How the remote fills the screen.
Ringomote finds Apple TVs on your Wi-Fi network with Bonjour and pairs with one the way an iPad does: it shows a code, you type it here. Nothing is sent beyond your network.
The Apple TV lists this phone as “%1$s”. Leave empty to use the phone’s own name. A new name takes effect when you pair again.
No Apple TV found. Check that the phone is on the same Wi-Fi network as the Apple TV.
The Apple TV is showing a 4-digit code. Enter it here.
Not paired. Pairing lets Ringomote control this Apple TV and turn it on when it sleeps.
Could not reach the Apple TV.
Could not connect to the Apple TV.
The Apple TV rejected the pairing. Check the code and try again; if Ringomote was removed on the Apple TV, just pair again.
%1$s is not connected. If it is asleep, wake it.
Wake-up sent to %1$s. It should connect in a moment.
Could not reach %1$s over the network.
%1$s no longer knows this pairing. Pair again under Settings.
Could not reach %1$s over Wi-Fi. Trying again.
%1$s no longer knows this pairing. Pair again under Settings.
Not connected. Pair Ringomote with an Apple TV under Settings.
Pair Ringomote with %1$s, as an iPad is, and it can control the Apple TV.
Use your phone as a remote for Apple TV, compatible with the Siri Remote (1st generation).

Ringomote collects no data and connects to no server. It looks for Apple TVs on your Wi-Fi network with Bonjour, and once you pair one, button presses go only to that Apple TV, directly over your network, encrypted with the pairing keys. The app stores only your settings and the pairing keys; the keys stay on the phone and are excluded from backups. Nothing is sent beyond your network.

Ringomote is built with AndroidX, Jetpack Compose, Material 3, Kotlin and kotlinx.coroutines, all under the Apache License 2.0. Its Wi-Fi status icon and the Menu and TV button icons use Google’s Material Icons (Apache License 2.0). Talking to the Apple TV over the network uses the Bouncy Castle crypto library (MIT-style Bouncy Castle License), following the protocol notes of the pyatv project, with its SRP login checked against srptools’ test vectors (BSD 3-Clause); no code from either is included.
